$do_not_edit: GENERATED. Edit the generator, never this file — the selftest asserts this file equals a fresh generation and a hand edit is a RED.
$what: The bento EDIT-PASS VOCABULARY: every dial Apollo's edit pass exposes, its option set, and where the defaults live. s219-D1(1): a bento role setting closes as a DEFAULT plus the EDIT-PASS OPTION SET.
$groundwork_only: No editor is built or proposed here. This is the vocabulary such an editor would read, minted when the vocabulary was ruled.

$permission_levels.$what: s219-D3(1): generation, editing and authoring are PERMISSION LEVELS on this one manifest, not three systems.
$permission_levels.generation: ships the minted defaults only — zero decisions up front, every generated instance lands on canon.
$permission_levels.editing: picks within these rails and cannot leave canon.
$permission_levels.authoring: the only mode that widens the rails — a new option or chord runs the gates and its promotion into this file is a governance act.
$permission_levels.$one_file: The library page, the editor-to-be and the generator all read THIS file, so none of the three can drift from the others (s219-D3(6)).

rail.quoted: Spacing rails are the ruled stop set {1, 2, 4, 16, 24, 40} - the edit pass picks among stops, never free values; widening the set is a ruling.

spacing.note: s219-D1(4): the edit pass picks among stops, never free values; widening the set is a ruling.

mainSpacing.note: s219-D1(4): the edit pass picks among stops, never free values; widening the set is a ruling. s217-D5's 'never tight' absence is retired by s219-D1(2) and now lives in the DEFAULT (24/40/40/24), not in the option space.

subSpacing.note: s219-D1(4): the edit pass picks among stops, never free values; widening the set is a ruling. The slider is driven in PIXELS and snapped to the nearest stop, ties to the lower stop; s217-D6's 1·2·4·8·12·16·20·24 ladder is superseded by the rail.

keylines.note: Available in every type and every theme (s219-D2(4)). The dashboard construction is s217-D8/#218: keylines hug the modules, the four corner tiles carry the sub-bento's radius.

mode.note: Gallery bento (canon's span grid) or justified rows.

edge.note: s219-D2(2) makes SQUARE the gallery-role default in all four themes; the dial stays. Surfaced only under mode=bento — a bottom edge is a property of the span grid, and justified rows have no ragged edge to square.

rounding.note: Never console-only: authored in all four themes, visibly different wherever the radius token is non-zero. s219-D2(3) defaults console gallery to capsule.

bentoBg.note: THE SECTION GROUND (s219-D3(5)). Takes any of the light or dark greys; a caption's ink is measured against the EFFECTIVE ground, which is this one whenever the caption is transparent.

capBg.note: Caption ground. s219-D2(1) supersedes s218-D6(1) for the DEFAULT: mono gallery captions resolve light grey. s219-D3(3) returns the dark ground as a chord OPTION, scoped console gallery — see exclusion X6, which is OPEN.

page_rail.$what: PAGE BACKGROUND IS NOT A BENTO DIAL. s219-D3(4): 'page background is a page-level general designer decision with its own small rail (white or the light greys in light mode; dark equivalents to be derived from tokens)'.
page_rail.$dark_equivalents: DERIVED, not chosen: every rail member is a token that already carries its own dark value, so no dark-specific decision was needed and none is PROPOSED.
page_rail.$rescope_note: The twelve shipped defaults spell the page ground grey/white/transparent. On a page body `transparent` never meant 'paint nothing' — it already compiled to --background-default (gen_foundations_217.page_bg_decl). The rail names that ground `page`; the map above sends the old word to it. Same declaration, same pixels. Receipts and exports under notes/ are FROZEN HISTORY and keep the old word.
page_rail.$collapse: `page` and `white` resolve to the SAME colour in LIGHT mode in all four themes and DIFFER in dark. Both are kept: the pair is a real distinction the tokens make. SURFACED, never swapped.

constraints.$what: s219-D3(2): OPTIONS COME IN CHORDS, NOT FREE DIALS. A chord settles several dials as a coherent set; ink follows ground automatically and is contrast-gated.

$ink_rule.$what: Ink is DERIVED from the ground, never picked. s219-D3(2).
$ink_rule.transparent: no ground of its own — the ink follows the EFFECTIVE ground (the bento's, then the page's)

chords.name: Capsule
chords.quoted: full capsule + caption ground from the grey ramp INCLUDING dark grey with reversed-out text
plain: The whole tile is one capsule.
The caption sits inside it, on a ground from the grey ramp.
Dark grey is on the ramp, and its text reverses out.
You choose the ground. The text colour follows it.

console/dark.from: #220 — Dave's pick on the caption-dark ladder: rgb(48,48,48) / #303030
console/dark.why: the shipped console-dark capsule caption ground resolves --surface-digital-black #1A1A1A, which IS the page ground (--background-default, console dark) — so the caption has no capsule to sit in. neutral/5 lifts it off the page.

chords.name: Rounded
chords.quoted: four rounded corners on images + transparent caption background
plain: Four rounded corners on the image.
The caption has no ground of its own.
Its text sits on whatever is behind — the wall, or the page.

exclusions.rule: capBg may not equal bentoBg unless it is transparent
exclusions.plain: A caption cannot sit on its own colour. Grey on grey has no edge.

exclusions.rule: rounding=capsule requires capBg != transparent OR keylines=on
exclusions.plain: A capsule needs an edge. Give the caption a ground, or turn keylines on.

exclusions.rule: the caption ink must be the token its effective ground implies (INK_FOR_GROUND)
exclusions.plain: Text colour is not a dial. It follows the ground underneath it.

exclusions.rule: every ground option must clear 4.5:1 against the ink its ground implies, in every theme and mode the chord is scoped to
exclusions.plain: Every ground on offer has to be readable. Anything under 4.5:1 is not offered.

exclusions.rule: the capsule and rounded chords are mutually exclusive
exclusions.plain: Capsule and Rounded are two answers to one question. Pick one.

exclusions.ruled_by: s219-D3(3) — Mono's access is EXPRESSLY OPEN
exclusions.rule: capBg=darkgrey is reachable only inside a chord that offers it, and today only console gallery has one
exclusions.plain: The dark caption ground belongs to the console capsule chord. Whether mono may have it is an open question for Dave — it is not refused on taste, it is simply not ruled yet.
exclusions.open_question: MONO'S ACCESS TO THE DARK-CAPTION CHORD. s219-D3(3) says it is EXPRESSLY OPEN and not ruled. Nothing here grants it: `capbg_for('gallery','mono')` does not carry `darkgrey`, and the refusal names this question as its reason rather than a preference. FOR DAVE.

constraints.$blocking_sweep: Every ground option of every chord is measured against the ink its ground implies, in light AND dark, in every theme the chord is scoped to. A reading under the floor is a selftest FAILURE, not a note (s219-D3(3): 'the CI sweep is blocking').

legality.rule: capBg may not equal bentoBg unless it is transparent
legality.why: a caption is judged against its IMMEDIATE ground

legality.rule: rounding=capsule requires capBg != transparent OR keylines=on
legality.why: a capsule with no edge is not a capsule

$reachable_note: The bento matrix, per theme. pageBg is NOT a factor: s219-D3(4) took it out of this grammar and it is counted on its own as `page_rail.options` (3). Console gallery is larger than the other three because s219-D3(3) scopes the dark caption ground to its capsule chord.

defaults.$owner: knowledge/_render/gen_foundations_217.py — s219-D1(3): the twelve verbatim exports are the shipped defaults, minted as concrete per-theme values at mint time (s200-D1). This module owns the OPTION SPACE, not the defaults.

$open_questions: MONO'S ACCESS TO THE DARK-CAPTION CHORD — s219-D3(3) says EXPRESSLY OPEN, not ruled. Nothing here grants it: `darkgrey` is not in mono's reachable caption grounds, exclusion X6 refuses it, and the refusal prints this question as its reason rather than a preference. FOR DAVE.

s219-D1(2) rules ALL dials available in every theme and ROLE. Enacted here as: no dial is locked BY THEME (the one theme lock, gallery-in-console keylines, is retired). Whether it also means a dashboard should carry a caption-background dial is NOT enacted — Dave's own twelve exports carry 5 dials for dashboard and 4 for display, and inventing a caption dial for a role with no captions would be reading past the exports. FOR DAVE.

s217-D5 ruled the dashboard main wall NEVER tight. s219-D1(2) puts every stop on every spacing dial, so 1px is now reachable there and 'never tight' survives only as the shipped default. FOR DAVE — an absence retired by implication, named rather than assumed.
